newsitem.title: USA: Argentina says US to allow fresh beef imports soon.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says US to allow fresh beef imports soon.

text.p: The United States will lift a 67-year-old ban on imports of fresh Argentine beef in the near future, likely in May, officials from both nations said Friday.
"We believe this will be in May," Argentine Agriculture Secretary Felipe Sola told reporters.
Sola also said his country's soybean crop "will be around 13 million (metric) tons."
"We have had a serious drought," Sola said.
Argentina will issue a new forecast for the crop in late May. Its latest official estimate was 13.8 million tonnes. USDA pegged the crop at 13.25 million tonnes earlier this month.
Sola said the crop would be between 13 million and 13.8 million tonnes.
Argentina has campaigned for three years for U.S. approval to utilize its quota of 20,000 tonnes of high-quality fresh beef.
The issue was under review at the White House budget office, Sola said.
"There are no objections being heard and it should be ready in the words of (U.S. Agriculture Secretary) Dan Glickman as soon as possible," Sola told reporters.
Glickman's trade adviser, Paul Drazek, in a separate session with reporters said, "May is definitely conceivable. The rule is making its way through the regulatory process."
Drazek said imports of 20,000 tonnes of fresh meat would have little impact on the U.S. cattle industry.
The United States banned fresh Argentine beef out of fear of foot-and-mouth disease in the early 1930s. Sola said the Argentine herd has been certified free of the disease for three years.
Sola said disagreements remained over access to U.S. markets for peanuts exported from Argentina.
